newsitem.title: UK: Japan hopes to sign up to Boca Raton accord.
newsitem.headline: Japan hopes to sign up to Boca Raton accord.

text.p: Japan is looking to become a signatory to the Boca Raton regulatory accord, if some of the rules on participation are eased, Hidehiro Konno, director-general of Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said.
"Japan plans to become a signatory to Boca Raton if qualification conditions are eased," Konno said at the International Derivatives Conference.
At present two Japanese ministries, as well as an agency in Singapore, are unable to sign up to the accord reached some two years ago in Boca Raton.
Under pacts reached there, some 55 exchanges share confidential information on large market positions, while umbrella agreements cover around 15 different regulator bodies.
Britain's Securities and Investments Board (SIB) and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) are looking at ways to ease participation in the Boca Raton accord, he said.

Konno was speaking on progress made since last November, when regulators and representatives from 17 countries responsible for regulating leading commodity markets met in London and agreed to strengthen supervision.
Konno, SIB Chairman Sir Andrew Large and CFTC Chairperson Brooksley Born, were the co-chairs of the London Commodity Futures Market Conference.
"We have started to update rules on commodities and now established a viable frame-work for information-sharing," he said.
Each country now has a contact person, who are already communicating and are ready to take action if needed, he said.
